item.text: {"text":"BERT4Rec establishes bidirectional masked-item learning; temporal attention is a possible extension, not evidence that recent interactions should dominate. [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) models pairwise time intervals alongside absolute positions, supporting elapsed-time information beyond sequence order, but uses a different backbone. [TLSTSRec](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.3233/IDA-240051), published online in 2024 and in a 2025 issue, combines temporal representations with adaptive long-/short-term preference fusion. These results motivate testing temporal features; they do not establish gains for the pinned Amazon benchmark or prove that time gaps identify current intent.\n\nA family-preserving hypothesis: add jointly learned, head-specific attention biases indexed by bucketed time gaps inside one BERT4Rec network, retaining masked-target training and appended-mask inference. This is an architectural inference from the literature, not a validated result. Avoid assuming monotonic preference decay; allow learned biases to retain older interests. The appended mask must use a timestamp convention available at inference, never the held-out interaction time. First repair ModelView category routing and verify candidate-score parity between the trained model and exported checkpoint/predictor, including final-nonpadding readout under left padding. Then compare temporal bias against the corrected baseline using fixed macro validation HR@10. History truncation or timestamp interventions can measure sensitivity after parity is established, but cannot alone establish causal preference changes."}
